research_boundary: Isolated contributor experiment only; leaves native PublicCausalCells, Amalgam checkpoint, accepted main, controller and owner runner unchanged.
question: Does bounded local spawn/prune/rewire of causal relationships improve intervention choice, out-of-family causal transfer and cold functional reuse compared with equally informed, trained, compute-budgeted fixed-topology and Bayesian causal models?
hypothesis: On previously unfamiliar interventions that discriminate competing causal rules, self-assembly should improve post-intervention net consequence reward after an A-B-A shift while keeping old functional readouts through process exit; retained bytes or a Bayesian tie alone are insufficient.
departure_from_gate27: Gate27 only compared predictions on externally selected actions from an in-family 56-XOR hypothesis universe; its archive had zero reward advantage over conventional controls. Gate28 makes the learner choose interventions and includes causal operators outside that universe; no Gate27 primary seeds will be reused as a new scientific trial.

world_plan.observation: 8 binary exogenous features, six candidate causal intermediate variables, one binary consequence with 10% label flips for non-noise cohorts
world_plan.interventions: 12 do(variable,value) choices, plus no-intervention/passive action. Chosen intervention, resulting observable state and binary consequence are public; true graph, family, phase, counterfactual outcomes and test labels remain hidden.
world_plan.regimes: A: 96 public randomized interventions for source grounding; B: 64 unannounced new causal rules and learner-selected interventions; R: 64 unannounced return-to-A learner-selected interventions. Stationary and independent-noise negative cohorts use identical counts.
world_plan.unknown_rule_family: A sources use pairwise XOR, AND, OR and negated gates; B shifted worlds include three-parent majority and two-stage mediated composition, potentially with one-step lag. All arms are given the same primitive operator dictionary; no hidden B label or hard-coded transition cue.
world_plan.held_queries: 32 never-exposed intervention-context queries at B endpoint and 32 at R endpoint per seed, scored in a separate read-only evaluator. Held queries/outcomes are never fed back.
world_plan.cold: Three fully exited Python subprocesses per seed, between source A, B, and R. Checkpoint must preserve a source capability and native decision function, not just byte hashes.
world_plan.randomness: Deterministic domain-separated seed streams for world graphs, action-feedback noise, fixed exposure, and held scoring. Reuse potential-outcome noise per seed/time across active policies where feasible; separate model policy RNG streams. No rerunning consumed primary seeds as fresh first-use.

arms: bounded local structural learner with at most 64 mutable edges and 16 cells; explicit spawn/prune/rewire events with auditable causes
same-capacity fixed-topology learner trained on the same interventions
same-capacity randomized rewiring with equal attempted edits
same-capacity surprise-gated rewiring without discriminating intervention value
fully trained causal Bayesian ensemble with the same declared primitive dictionary and measured inference budget
Bayesian expected-information-gain intervention planner with same dictionary and action budget

fairness.active_policy: Compare independently chosen actions under equal per-world intervention counts and identical hidden worlds; because actions differ, do NOT claim matched information for active-policy reward.
fairness.forced_action: Additional externally selected equal-action/equal-observation replay of every arm isolates learned-model quality from exploration differences; report separately, never blend with active-policy results.
fairness.compute: Limit each arm to 8192 primitive rule evaluations per intervention and <=16384 serialized state bytes; account for all source fit, update, selection and held scoring. Publish actual work/time/memory and strongest unconstrained Bayesian reference as a secondary upper bound. If a strong control cannot be meaningfully trained within the declared budget, science remains UNVERIFIED; do not cherry-pick weak controls.
fairness.calibration: All thresholds, hyperparameters, grammar, causal world generator, evaluator, identities, and model selection must be frozen by a separate committed code/config revision before the first primary run; no scoring permitted from this preregistration alone.
fairness.overhead: No paid models, production secrets, operator runner, scheduler or uncontrolled external tools.

metrics.primary: For 48 shifted paired seeds: R-phase mean net action-consequence reward and B+R cumulative intervention regret versus the strongest matched conventional trained control. 95% paired confidence intervals computed across seeds, not across repeated held queries.
metrics.secondary: Held B/R intervention-conditioned probability Brier, unfamiliar mediated/majority causal edge/intervention-choice accuracy, A functional source readout after interference and cold restart, spurious rewires on stationary worlds, calibration and excess certainty on independent noise, rule evaluation and CPU cost.
metrics.negative_controls: Stationary non-shift and causally independent outcome noise; remove source archive and intervention-value selection; random rewiring and fixed-structure mechanism ablations.
metrics.action_cost: All 13 actions have equal charged cost 1; no claim of energy efficiency based solely on abstract rule-evaluation count.

evidence_order: 1. This preregistration receives its own immutable commit before any primary scoring.
2. Implement source, world generator, complete trained controls, per-action accounting and evaluator. Freeze all at a different exact commit before ANY primary outcome.
3. Run ONE new primary first-use on committed code, with source SHA and workflow run/job IDs; never classify later replay as new science.
4. Seal result.json and provenance.json in a later commit; run independent numerical audit.
5. Complete source-atlas update and complete exact-head Linux and Windows repository regression; do not confuse engineering failures with scientific negatives.
6. Preserve negative/consumed trials; keep draft/unmerged; native owner must separately qualify any integration.

classification_rules.engineering: Source-pinned full Linux+Windows unittest, code atlas, complete prior Gates10-27 frozen replay and new Gate28 audit pass on final candidate.
classification_rules.supported: All predeclared scientific thresholds pass on original first-use, with all matched arms implemented and actually trained; still an isolated synthetic contributor result requiring independent native owner reproduction.
classification_rules.mixed: Retention/structural adaptation passes but any causal value, transfer, calibration or negative control fails; no promotion.
classification_rules.negative: No positive significant action-consequence gain over the strongest conventional matched control, or negative safety/calibration control fails.
classification_rules.invalid: Primary result before fully frozen generator+source+evaluator; untrained/underbudgeted strongest control; insufficient matched evidence/compute; hidden labels or counterfactual leak; after-result parameter selection; ambiguous provenance.

status: PREREGISTERED DESIGN ONLY; model source, generator, code identity, first-use and scientific result NOT YET QUALIFIED.
